doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Jail and trial in Japan, October 1966 to February 1967
summary: Keiko and Elvin describe his detention, the trial, karate lessons from a guard and the deportation.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: That’s tragic. I had never heard this before. So then what happens now? Keiko comes to see you and you’re handcuffed at the airport?
(Keiko inaudible)
So they have you handcuffed, and what do they put you in Japanese prison? So what the rest of the tour goes back to the states?

Yes! He did this for the hearing for the not guilty. He didn’t! So I was in another city and I don’t know nothing about what is going on. I was contact promoter’s assistant. His name Akamica and he say, “You gotta’ come up” and it was December and I was so busy with my father so I have excuse. Ask my father, “I have to ride in to Tokyo.” I saw him and he didn’t see me cause after that, thank god he say, “That’s number 11C, Mr. Jones.” That’s the first time I’ve ever been to jail anyways (inaudible) then I spoke to the promoter and I say, “Listen, I’m sorry Elvin is lost” so (inaudible) I almost scream at this promoter. (Inaudible) Once you get deported you can never come back! Elvin got deported February 7th, 1967. (Inaudible) So I went to Tokyo to see the ambassador. American Consult to tell to these guys (Inaudible).
So, thank you so much. So she sees you, so how long were you detained in Japan.
October 31 to February 7th.
Yeah.
You were in a Japanese jail that long?
Well first I was in… I went to prison to wait for the trail and after the trial I was deported. So I went to the immigration people.
Still under Japanese authority or were you placed under American authority?
Oh no, I was under Japanese authority. That was Japan.
Okay.
One of the guards he wanted me to get some exercise. And he let me out of the cell and he said, “I’m going to show you how to play Karate.” And he was giving me Karate lessons.

After the trial he has to stay in the jail, I say, “No way.” So we, I and the promoter, work together and to get release for him. So then he’s got a free, and he stay, and we at hotel. And then that’s the reason why he works with Japanese musicians
(Inaudible).
They found him guilty again, so the appeal was guilty again?
Then I was in Japan and I was in Nagasaki and they say, “he’s gotta deport” and I say, “When?” and they say “tomorrow.”
Well I lost a good set of drums; I know that, I don’t know what happened to them. Somebody stole them.
(Inaudible)
That’s Art Blakey with his lying ass! (Laughs)
